summary: Fumio Shoji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Rissho University. He served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University around 2013.
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University from around 1954 to 1958 and later held a post there from around 1970 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae works in Indology and philosophy. He was a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991) and later held posts at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies (attested 1997) and Shimane International Junior College (attested 1998).

Futoshi Takehashi, a Buddhist studies scholar, completed doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992). From 1995 to 1997, he served as a research assistant at the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies.

Fyodor Buslaev (1818–1897) specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University from around 1834 to 1838 and held a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Saint Petersburg under Minaev and Oldenburg, and under Bühler and Jacobi, he was a professor at the University of Saint Petersburg from around 1900 to 1942.

Félix Nève (1816–1893) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at KU Leuven and under Lassen, Thiersch, and Burnouf, he served as professor and later professor emeritus at KU Leuven (Catholic University of Louvain) between 1841 and 1877.
G. Srinivasa Murti was an Indologist who served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1938–1949 and 1971).

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), served as vice president of the Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and was an adjunct professor of English at Columbia University (around 1978–2006).
G. V. Aston is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Paul Harrison and earned a PhD in philosophy from the University of Canterbury between 1986 and 2004.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945 and retired from the office of the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin M. Nagao (1907–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, later holding the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971).

Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He worked at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute around 1950–1963 and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University around 1963–1981.

Galmangoda Sumanapala is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) and as Senior Professor and Director at the University of Kelaniya (attested 2012).

Galsang Gomboev (1818–1863) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and taught Mongolian at the University of Saint Petersburg from 1855 to 1863.

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Peradeniya and University of Washington. A religious and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Ceylon, Washington, UC San Diego, and was Emeritus Professor of Anthropology at Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He served as department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1905, and held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1917–1923) and the University of Calcutta (~1914–1935).

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) studied at Allahabad, Calcutta, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He was a professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1918–1923), and vice chancellor of the University of Allahabad (1923–1932).
